description:
WHAT IT IS MADE OF. Every token is built from the same three flat vector layers over a flat near-black charcoal ground (no texture, no gradient, no vignette). (1) A DOT layer: solid circles in a very dark umber, barely above the ground in value, arranged as a loose ring or scattered arc around the centre - a top arc, left and right flanks at mid-height, a bottom arc. In most seeds they are small and half-buried; in 10801 they are large and laid out as an almost regular grid-ring, and there they become the loudest thing in the frame. (2) A BAR layer: horizontal, flat-ended, hard-edged strips stacked at varying pitch and varying length, centred on a vertical axis so the stack reads as roughly bilaterally symmetric. They are semi-transparent and lighten what they cross, so they over-print the other layers like a scan line, a venetian blind, or a barcode. Their colours run from pale sand through khaki to a mid grey-olive. (3) A SHARD layer: saturated amber/ochre quadrilaterals - rotated rectangles, blades, planks, splinters - overlapping each other around the centre, their overlaps building up brighter. This is the only saturated colour in the work and it is always the focal mass.

WHAT IT IS A PICTURE OF. Nothing literal. It reads as an object caught behind a shutter: an amber cluster - sometimes a shield or arrowhead (9011, 9369), sometimes an exploded starburst of blades (9548, 10085, 10264), sometimes a few thrown sticks (9190, 10443, 10980) - seen through horizontal interference. The strongest associations are a struck spark or ember behind window slats, a torn poster, and a scan or interlace glitch over a solid form. The 512 single is the clearest statement of it: an amber arrowhead pointing down, a tight square of pale slats across its middle, a dark ring of dots orbiting it in a large empty black field.

WHAT THE TWELVE SHARE. One palette family and no second hue anywhere - amber, sand, khaki, grey-olive, umber, black. One ground. The same three layers in the same stacking order. The same centred, axis-symmetric placement: every seed puts its mass in the middle of the frame and lets the ground carry the margin. The same hard-edged, flat, no-stroke, no-outline drawing language.

HOW THEY DIFFER. Almost entirely by the RATIO of bar to shard and by scale. Three registers are visible. BAR-DOMINANT: 9906, 10443 and 10622 are nearly filled by wide grey and tan slats that run off both edges, with the amber reduced to a subordinate tangle (in 10443 the amber is thin scratchy lines and is nearly lost). SHARD-DOMINANT: 9548, 10264 and 10085 are amber starbursts with only a light bar wash across them. COMPACT: 9011, 9369 and 10801 are small tight forms floating in a lot of black, with a modest bar stack; 10801 is the outlier of the set, a small amber knot ringed by big dark discs and hardly any bars. 9190 and 10980 are the sparse thrown-stick reading. Densities range from very open (9369) to nearly saturated (9906), which is a wide but still legibly related spread.

WHAT HAPPENS ACROSS THE THREE STATES. The bar layer carries almost all of it, and the direction is consistent across all four state seeds. NEUTRAL is a mid-pitch stack of moderate bars. STRESS strips the stack down to a few THICK, widely spaced, greyer, more opaque slabs - the frame opens up, the amber body is exposed between heavy horizontal slabs, and the whole tile reads coarser and dimmer (9011 stress and 9369 stress are the clearest: 9369 loses most of its bars and most of its bottom dot arc). RECOVERY inverts it: many MORE, much FINER, paler and brighter lines, the densest and lightest of the three, and the dot ring repopulates (9369 recovery regains a full top and bottom arc of dots). The amber mass also brightens slightly from stress to recovery, and in 9548 and 9190 the shard geometry itself shifts a little between states - blades spread wider and re-angle - though never enough to change what the token is. Read as a sentence: coarse and broken under stress, finely re-knit and brighter under recovery.

IDENTITY ACROSS STATES. Strong. 9011 keeps its downward amber arrowhead in all three, 9190 its crossed scaffold of long sticks, 9369 its small compact body, 9548 its starburst. No seed becomes a different object; the changes are to texture, count, pitch and brightness, not to the subject.

WHAT SURVIVES AT 120PX. The amber mass and its silhouette survive completely - it is high contrast against black and it is what you actually read. The bar layer survives as texture rather than as individual bars, and that is enough for the state read: at 120 the stress row is visibly a few heavy slabs, the recovery row is visibly a fine haze, and neutral sits between (9011 and 9369 are unmistakable at this size; 9190 is subtler; 9548 is the weakest - its three states are all a dense amber mass and only the internal texture separates them). The dot layer is essentially GONE at 120 in every seed except 10801, and to a lesser degree 9190 and 10264 - it is too dark against the ground to register at browse size, so a whole layer of the work is invisible where the collection is actually seen. The twelve still read as twelve things at 120, but they separate mainly by density and by bar-to-amber ratio; the middle group (9727, 9906, 10085, 10980) converges toward a similar impression of an amber tangle inside a horizontal stack.

ARTIFACTS I NOTICED BEFORE JUDGING. Bars run off the left and right frame edges and are cut by the viewBox in 9906, 10443 and 10622 - it reads as deliberate bleed rather than error, but in 10443 the bottom-most pale bar is a full-width slab that hits both edges and flattens the composition. Several dots are clipped at the frame edge (9011 lower left, 9727 left). Bar-on-bar overlaps in 9906 and 10622 produce a banded moire where three or four values interleave. Nothing reads as a rendering failure.
